clue.text: Shares two pints with Queen and son

parts.note: a quart is a measure of two pints
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A drinker splits a couple of pints with royalty and her boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarters are portions of a whole, so they are shares divided out among people.

parts.note: ails means troubles or afflicts

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is bothering the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Quails are small plump game birds of the partridge family.

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
diction is the manner of speaking

explanation.surface: Observe a verbal tic someone has.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependency, a habit one cannot easily break.

clue.text: Beat king with small military units

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
K is the chess abbreviation for king
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A monarch defeats an enemy with a few little army detachments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'units' points to soldiers, but here it means armoured vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanks are armoured fighting vehicles, each one a unit of military hardware.

clue.text: Tops up studies involving left overs

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so other letters go inside

parts.note: reads means studies, as at university
O stands for overs on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: Someone refills while reviewing the leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left overs' looks like leftover food; it splits into L and O, the cricket scorecard's abbreviation for overs, a set of six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload is to refill a weapon or container, so to top it up again.

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters are handled and arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: The boss oversaw the smooth running of the workflow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a steady current, as of water or traffic, a synonym of a flow.

clue.text: Four identical notes about a meeting

indicators.note: about means going round, so the notes surround the single letter

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, used four times

explanation.surface: A melody of four repeated notes plays round a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two people, an intimate encounter.

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A severe painter who breaks the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Max Ernst was a German Surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a Dada and Surrealist painter, a famous twentieth-century artist.

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
stress means strain or pressure

explanation.surface: A tense note is passed to a secret partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress is a woman in a long-term affair, a man's female lover.

clue.text: Perhaps painting outside of study with heartless lady fervently

indicators.note: outside of tells us one word wraps around the other here

parts.note: painting is one example of art, hence the 'perhaps'
a den is a private study room

indicators.note: heartless strips the inner letters from the word lady, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: An art student and a woman with no feelings working passionately together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps painting' signals an example of a broader category; 'outside of' wraps one piece around the other, and 'heartless' keeps only the ends of 'lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: To act ardently is to act with passion and zeal, the same as fervently.

clue.text: Bears in street with last of zookeepers

parts.note: and means with, joining things together

indicators.note: last of picks just the final letter of the word zookeepers

explanation.surface: Bears roam a street alongside the final zookeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals of the surface, but it is the verb meaning tolerates.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to put up with it, just as one bears an annoyance.

indicators.note: oddly deficient means lacking the odd-numbered letters, keeping the even ones of Obtained

explanation.surface: Someone got hold of a poorly made strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a strip encircling something, like a belt round the waist.

definitions.meaning: to fasten a door with a key is to make it fast
tresses or curls of hair on the head

explanation.surface: Someone fixes their hairstyle in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock fastens a door, and locks are also tresses or strands growing on the head.

clue.text: A dog getting flower and stone

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador retriever
an aster is a daisy-like garden bloom

explanation.surface: A dog in a garden among blooms and rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a smooth white mineral carved for ornaments, a kind of stone.

indicators.note: in an across clue east is the right, so the first letter travels to the end of the word

parts.note: slight means slim or thin

explanation.surface: A lean figure heads east and lights the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head moving east' takes the S at the front of SLIGHT and sends it to the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: To light something is to shine on it so it can be seen, to illuminate it.

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after, so the asking word follows

parts.note: airs means broadcasts on radio or TV
pray means to ask or request

explanation.surface: A man's show is put out on the radio by listener demand.
explanation.walkthrough: Hairspray is a Broadway musical set in 1960s Baltimore.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairspray is a stage and screen musical about a teenager joining a TV dance show.

clue.text: Daughter urges page to drop off clothes

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: drop off tells us one letter falls away from the word before

parts.note: presses means urges or pushes someone

explanation.surface: A daughter pushes a page boy to strip off his clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here: to clothe someone is to dress them.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a person is to put garments on them, which is to clothe them.

clue.text: Cut a sleep out to reflect

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Skip a nap so you can think things over.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to ponder or muse, to reflect on possibilities.

clue.text: Scrap with priest over English falsehood

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a whit is the smallest scrap or bit
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A fight with a cleric about an English lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight, but it means a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A white lie is a harmless or polite untruth, a minor falsehood.

indicators.note: around signals one word sitting on both sides of the other

parts.note: hung means hovered or floated in the air
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Searching for scrap metal that drifted about.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting means searching for or seeking, the same as looking for.

indicators.note: carrying means the phrase holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Staging a heist while carrying the kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is equipment or tackle for a job, a set of tools.

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the central letter of the seven-letter synonym

parts.note: pierces means stabs through

explanation.surface: A cruel attacker stabs muscular men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' drops the R at the centre of PIERCES; 'hunks' are chunks, not attractive men.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunks are large chunks or portions of something, which are pieces of it.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: slots means puts something into place

explanation.surface: A detective raises his weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols are handguns, which are firearms or arms.

indicators.note: filled with means the ship's letters contain another word

parts.note: an air is a tune or tone

explanation.surface: A steamer rocks in a breezy sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' could be a verb for the ship's motion, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Stones are small pieces of rock, so rocks in the plural.

indicators.note: holding means the jumble keeps another letter inside it
involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Devil worship involves keeping big protective charms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SATANISM, and 'holding' puts L inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil, and a talisman is the same lucky object.

parts.note: the middle letters of the name Elsa are an el and an ess, which written as a phrase joins them with a conjunction

explanation.surface: Wins the love of a girl called Elsa.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a phrase of two letters joined by 'and': those two letters make up the middle of Elsa.
explanation.definitionFit: To land something is to secure or win it, like landing a job or a fish.

definitions.meaning: to regard or reckon someone as something
a European nobleman of rank equal to an earl

explanation.surface: Think about whether an aristocrat is important.
explanation.definitionFit: We reckon someone a friend, an earl's continental equal holds this title, and what is important carries weight.

clue.text: Prisoner has endless space to dance

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off the word for a space

parts.note: a gap is a space

explanation.surface: An inmate with room to spare starts dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance in which people follow in single file.

parts.note: a line is a brand or range of goods

indicators.note: outside of picks the two outer letters of the word regions

explanation.surface: Ships carry a brand name beyond their home waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Liners are large passenger vessels, such as ocean-going ships.

clue.text: Infant dancing across old university water feature

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the jumble spans the other letters
dancing suggests the letters jigging about into a new order

explanation.surface: A toddler dances around in an old college's ornamental pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges INFANT, and 'across' sets it around O and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountain is a decorative jet of water in a garden or square, a classic ornamental water display.

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word Mensa, the second and fourth

parts.note: says means announces or declares

explanation.surface: The high-IQ society keeps declaring new exams.
explanation.walkthrough: Mensa is a society for people who score highly on intelligence tests.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt or trial, an old sense of a test, as in essaying a task.

clue.text: SS surrounding point to get runaways

indicators.note: surrounding means the spelled letters sit on either side of the headland

parts.note: each S is written out by its letter name, ess, giving two of them
a cape is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: Nazi guards close in on a spot where fugitives are caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to spell out each S of 'SS' by its letter name rather than reading the Nazi unit; 'surrounding' then puts the headland between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapees are people who have broken free and fled, which is what runaways are.
